tagline: Back roads on both banks of the Pee Dee.
intro: The byway starts on US 52 a couple of miles north of Ansonville and takes Pinkston River Road and Grassy Island Road toward the Pee Dee River through pine and hardwood forest, swamp and farm. NC 109 carries it north and over into Richmond County, where a second Grassy Island Road runs twelve miles more to Holly Grove Church Road, a few miles west of Ellerbe. Near the end the low Piedmont begins to rise toward the Uwharries.
The byway takes its name from Grassy Island, a cluster of earthen masses in the river north of Blewett Falls Lake.

moments.title: Ansonville
moments.text: Settled in 1844 about a mile west of the Pee Dee, the town once had a college for the daughters of local planters, which the Civil War closed.

moments.title: Pee Dee National Wildlife Refuge
moments.text: Set aside in 1963 for wintering geese and ducks, the refuge sits a few hundred yards from Lockhart Gaddy's private goose pond, which wintered more than 10,000 Canada geese a year in the 1950s.

moments.title: Blewett Falls Lake
moments.text: A hydropower dam drowned the old Blewett Falls of the Pee Dee early in the 1900s, and along the lake's 34 miles of shoreline no bridge crosses it.
